title: What the band needed from a pianist, and hiring Russell Robinson
summary: He explains pianists had to play bass and countermelody, and says Robinson fit the rhythm.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: And, uh, I hate to ask this. This is embarrassing to him, I know, but what did you require of a piano player that he couldn't play?

They could not play the rhythm. I see. They couldn't get the rhythm. As simple as you think it was, not even Al Menard who was the greatest piano player on the American stage. He couldn't fit with us. He disrupted the band. Each one of them, they played a different kind of rhythm than we played. It was not until the records come out that these fellows began to decipher and know what our success was from the rhythm.
Did your piano play just the straight chords?

Play chords and he played bass, played bass and contramelody. We were able to fill in. In other words, he'd have to know the rhythm twice, play the chords, and he played bass too. You see, there was bass hand. And the other one he played, contramelodies, no melody. All contramelodies and harmonies. And that's what he was to play. And I couldn't get to these fellows. All they played bird music up on top of the piano. Bird music. There was no foundation tone and they disrupt the band. Now, along comes Robinson. He comes in the hotel. I was staying at that time at the Pontchartrain Hotel, now called Wilson Hotel. They have changed the name again. That was in the back of Ryzenweather. He heard that from going around the music publishing, he heard we needed a piano piano. And I said, yeah. I said, can you feel it? He says, I think I can. He says, me and my brother was going around to picture shows as an added attraction. Playing in the picture shows along with your records. I played the piano, my brother played the drums. And he used to think it was a whole band. We had a great big photograph, a great big heart on it. And that's how he learned the tunes. I went over to Ryzenweather's that afternoon with him. And I heard him play. He played it better than anybody that I'd ever heard play before. I says, all right, you want the job? I said, yeah. But he filled in for Ryzenweather's two theater jobs we had. One was in Brooklyn, one was in New York. And we leave for London, England. When we got to London, England.
